transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-20 11:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Dr. Ethan Cole (CTO - Nova Clinic), Maya Li (Head of Data - Nova), Samir Patel (Security), Jules Ramos (PM)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Quick POC scoping focused on data handling: PII classification, logging/redaction, retention settings, prompt storage concerns; agree pilot success criteria (latency, cost, quality), sample size for benchmarks, and timeline. Redwood to share security docs and run benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda: data handling during the POC, what Nova needs from a compliance perspective, and how we'll run benchmarks - latency, cost, and quality.
[00:14] Ethan: yep thanks Alex. for context, we're building an assistant for scheduling and chart summarization; the POC scope is 3 endpoints: extraction, summarization, and reranking. main concerns are PII leaving our systems and logs retention.
[00:30] Priya: great, and just to call out, typical Redwood pilot is we do a constrained benchmark with both hosted and private variants to show tradeoffs. we'll need sample traffic profile and a representative dataset.
[00:45] Maya: we'd prefer hosted for speed but security needs may force private. we are SOC2 in-flight and have strict retention policy - default must be 30 days for logs unless we opt out.
[00:58] Samir: important: we want proof that prompts are not persisted in plaintext, ability to redact or not log specific tokens, and KMS-backed encryption for any stored artifacts. also SSO/SAML and audit logs are non-negotiable.
[01:15] Alex: understood. for prompts and responses we have two options in Redwood: 1) transient mode - no prompt storage, ephemeral KV, no logs kept beyond ephemeral traces for debugging and 2) default with configurable retention and redaction rules. both support KMS integration for at-rest encryption.
[01:36] Jules: when you say transient mode is debugging possible - like if the model behaves wrong, how do you triage?
[01:44] Priya: good question. we capture minimal traces in a secure ledger when transient is on - that ledger is accessible only to your team via private deployment or via a short-lived debug export. it's intentionally limited and can be redacted client-side before upload.
[02:03] Ethan: ok that helps. what's the redaction capability? are there built-in PII detectors?
[02:09] Priya: we have heuristics + ML-based PII detection; typical flow is automatic redaction of common PII (SSNs, credit card, phone, email) plus a prompt-based rule engine so you can mark phrases or fields not to be stored. note detection isn't perfect - we recommend a pre-redaction step on your side for anything regulated.
[02:29] Maya: so we would anonymize at source and then Redwood applies a second pass? that sounds like our desired pattern.
[02:35] Priya: yes, double-layer. for the POC we can help tune the detectors on sample data.
[02:42] Samir: retention windows - can we set sub-daily retention? our security needs are 0 retention for raw prompts and 30 days for aggregated metrics only.
[02:52] Alex: short answer: yes. retention is configurable per-route. you can set 0 for prompt payloads and 30 days for aggregated logs/metrics. we also support auto-deletion policies and audit log exports.
[03:06] Jules: are prompts used to train models? that's a big concern for privacy and vendor risk.
[03:12] Alex: Redwood does not use customer prompts to train public models. for hosted customers, we have an opt-out and an explicit data use policy; for Dedicated and Private, there's zero training use by default. we'll put that in the security annex.
[03:25] Ethan: good. next: pilot success criteria - what does Redwood suggest?
[03:30] Priya: typical success criteria for Nova's use case: 1) latency p50/p95 under your SLO (you said target 300ms p95 for extraction?) 2) quality thresholds - F1 or ROUGE delta compared to baseline less than X, 3) cost per 1k requests under target, 4) no PII leakage in sample audit.
[03:50] Maya: yes 300ms p95 is our goal for extraction; summarization can be higher, up to 1s p95. quality: we will provide a labeled eval set to measure F1 for extraction and human eval for summarization.
[04:04] Priya: perfect. for workload sizing we need expected qps, average tokens per request, and concurrency. Jules?
[04:12] Jules: forecast: 50 qps peak, avg 120 tokens per request for extraction, summarization variable 300-800 tokens, concurrency up to 80 in bursts. pilot realistic workload can be 5-10 qps sustained.
[04:30] Priya: that helps. we'll size a pilot using a small dedicated instance and a hosted profile to compare. we'll report throughput, latency, and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:41] Samir: benchmarks - we want a reproducible harness and access to raw logs (redacted) to verify no PII. are you able to run the benchmark in our VPC?
[04:52] Alex: yes, options: hosted Redwood (we run in our cloud), Redwood Dedicated for reserved pools, or Redwood Private where we install in your VPC/on-prem. For the pilot, most customers do a hosted baseline then run a private pilot if security requires. we can run benchmark agents from your VPC if we provision a short-term service account.
[05:11] Ethan: cost - what's the expected ballpark for this pilot? not the final pricing but a guess so leadership knows.
[05:17] Alex: a pilot typically runs at a discounted rate; ballpark for our small dedicated pilot is low thousands per week depending on run time. we'll put exact numbers in the proposal.
[05:28] Maya: prompt storage concerns: we want to avoid storing full prompt text and instead store embeddings + hashes for dedupe. is that available?
[05:38] Priya: yes - you can configure to store only hashed prompts and embeddings for cache hits, and disable raw prompt retention. embeddings are encrypted with customer-managed KMS where required.
[05:48] Samir: and audit trails - do you have immutable audit logs and export to our SIEM?
[05:52] Alex: yep syslog/Splunk/CloudWatch exports, plus an append-only audit log we can stream to your S3 or SIEM. logs can be redacted or masked before export per rules.
[06:05] Jules: timeline - we want a 4-week pilot: week 0 setup and data handoff, week 1 benchmark run, week 2 tuning, week 3 evaluation and decision. feasible?
[06:15] Priya: feasible if we get sample data by 2026-06-23 and kickoff the benchmark week of 2026-06-29.
[06:23] Maya: okay we'll aim to deliver sample set by 6/23.
[06:26] Ethan: any regulatory issues for PHI? we're HIPAA-covered; need BAAs and on-prem options.
[06:33] Alex: we have HIPAA-compliant flows for Private deployments and BAAs available for Dedicated/Private. Hosted can be done under BAA for certain customers - we'll confirm specifics in the security packet.
[06:45] Samir: last item - can we redact in-flight text client-side before sending? we might want to mask patient names at the client layer and then send for summarization.
[06:55] Priya: absolutely. client-side redaction is the recommended best practice. Redwood can provide SDK snippets and a small library to help with deterministic masking and hashing so you can still do dedupe without sending raw names.
[07:12] Alex: great. recap of next steps: Alex shares security docs and data use policy; Priya sends benchmark plan; Maya provides anonymized sample data; schedule kickoff.
[07:24] Jules: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:28] Ethan: thanks all.
[07:30] Alex: we'll follow up via email, dropping links to the docs and a proposed timeline.

End of transcript.
